newsitem.title: USA: N. Dakota insured flood damage estimated $200 mln.
newsitem.headline: N. Dakota insured flood damage estimated $200 mln.

text.p: Damage from the floods that struck North Dakota in April will cost U.S. insurers at least $200 million, an industry trade group said.
The majority of the insured damage was to large commercial properties and to automobiles, said Property Claim Services, an industry-supported group that tracks insurance losses.
PCS said its estimate of insured damage may rise in coming weeks as more people return to their homes and businesses and and begin to file claims, PCS said.
PCS said its damage estimate was for North Dakota only and said it did not identify any other states as areas likely to report catastrophic levels of insured losses.

However, St. Paul Cos Inc last week said it expects damage from the flooding in the Red River Valley in Minnesota and North Dakota to result in pre-tax catastrophe losses of $30 million to $40 million in the second quarter.
